scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: The display says one litre, and you pay for exactly that. But how does the pump actually know?

scenes.name: pump
scenes.text: A motor pumps fuel up from a big tank, buried under the forecourt.

scenes.name: meter
scenes.text: The fuel passes through a flow meter. In many pumps, pistons fill and empty fixed chambers. A known volume, every stroke.

scenes.name: pulse
scenes.text: Each turn of the meter shaft triggers a pulser, sending electrical pulses. A fixed number of pulses equals a set volume.

scenes.name: calc
scenes.text: The pump's computer counts the pulses, converts them to litres, and multiplies by the price per litre.

scenes.name: seal
scenes.text: Legal metrology officials test pumps with a certified five litre measure, then seal the meter, so it can't be quietly tampered with.

scenes.name: tip
scenes.text: In India, you can ask for that five litre test at the pump. It's your right.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Meter, pulses, math, seal. Every drop counted. Follow for more on how things really work.
